request_state.literature: Literature (primary source arXiv:2412.11933, survey of solved cases): fully solved with all exponents>=3 are (3,3,n) for n<=10^9, (n,n,3) for n>=3, (n,n,n) for n>=3. Effective-finiteness only (not solved): (2p,2q,r) with p,q>=V_r [arXiv:2509.21083]. NOT solved: (4,4,5), (4,4,7), (4,6,3), any (2m,2n,r odd) with m!=n, (3,5,7), (5,5,7).
request_state.claim: Complete mod-8 analysis of a Beal counterexample, covering every parity configuration. C even: both exponents even is IMPOSSIBLE; x even with y odd forces B = 7 mod 8; both odd forces 8 | A+B. A even (so B, C odd): y,z both odd forces B = C mod 8; y odd with z even forces B = 1 mod 8. By symmetry the same holds with A and B exchanged.
